Nope, connected, then headers catch up, then it says beam block import is starting, then silence I am guessing it's on my side somehow, just combing through the logs ah, yeah, there are no rewards so the beams should be immediate I think the state root is the same at block 100k as at block 0 We do try to download the block signer's account info, whether or not there's a reward. But I don't see why that should be a problem it is I even wanted to mention this specifically It is in the document I shared Miner account (to update the miner balance with the tx fee payments and block reward) o It is not necessary in case of some consensus mechanisms where block reward is zero and block has no transactions for the wit protocol to work fine we should generally agree on what we touch and what we do not touch and there are some non-obvious cases 1) do we touch a miner account when no reward and zero gas price are paid 2) do we touch SELFDESTRUCT recipient accounts if the transfer value is zero 3) do we touch precompile account if the value is zero <@!489256758989029405> I've just updated the IDs of the [Get]BlockWitnessHashes in our implementation. let me know when you've updated yours updated node is running with the new version <@!489256758989029405> I'm now being disconnected all the time hmm, seems to be immediately after I send a GetBlockWitnessHashes msg yep, it's definitely that msg that is causing your node to disconnect for some reason using id 0 for GetBlockWitnessHashes I don't get disconnected, but never get a reply either checking I wiped the database to decrease the number of blocks to sync I am receiving responses when sending requests now I made a minor change (which I believe should have no impact) but it seems it may have ok, I can explain it now -> I did not update the MessageSpaceLength and the response messages were dropped sorry for that added regression test for this so it does not cause trouble when we introduce more messages to the protocol in the future > It is in the document I shared Sorry, which doc? > for the wit protocol to work fine we should generally agree on what we touch and what we do not touch > and there are some non-obvious cases > 1) do we touch a miner account when no reward and zero gas price are paid > 2) do we touch SELFDESTRUCT recipient accounts if the transfer value is zero > 3) do we touch precompile account if the value is zero Yeah, I agree, I suspect we are okay to not consider any of those as touched, for the sake of the witness. Though even if we disagree on that, Trinity considers the witness information as auxiliary, and runs the basic beam sync anyway. So even if the witness is smaller than Trinity expects, beam sync should work anyway, just slower.
